solution:
The product in the recurrence's numerator suggests taking reciprocals, which will separate the two preceding terms. Define \(b_n=1/a_n\). Then
\[
b_n=\frac{2a_{n-2}-a_{n-1}}{a_{n-2}a_{n-1}}
=\frac{2}{a_{n-1}}-\frac{1}{a_{n-2}}
=2b_{n-1}-b_{n-2}.
\]
Rearranging gives
\[
b_n-b_{n-1}=b_{n-1}-b_{n-2}.
\]
Thus the reciprocals form an arithmetic sequence. Its first two terms are \(1\) and \(7/3\), so its common difference is
\[
\frac73-1=\frac43.
\]
Therefore
\[
b_{2019}=1+2018\cdot\frac43
=\frac{3+8072}{3}
=\frac{8075}{3},
\]
and hence
\[
a_{2019}=\frac{3}{8075}.
\]
The digits of \(8075\) sum to \(20\), so \(8075\) is not divisible by \(3\). The fraction is already in lowest terms, and
\[
p+q=3+8075=\boxed{8078}.
\]
The answer is choice \(\mathrm{E}\).

\[

\]

\[
\frac73-1=\frac43.
\]

\[

edges.reason: The reciprocal is characterized by a product equal to one; negative rational reciprocals use the sign of that product.

A recurrence expresses a later term through earlier ones. That only makes sense once a sequence is understood as an ordered list with definite positions, so computing terms step by step depends on it.
edges.scope: ordered terms referenced by previous and next index

edges.reason: The target explicitly distinguishes a recurrence relation from a general-term formula; the latter's index-to-term meaning is part of this comparison.
edges.scope: distinguishing recurrence formulas from general term formulas

edges.reason: Evaluating the arithmetic general term at a specified n uses the meaning of an index substituted into a general-term expression.
edges.scope: substituting an index into the arithmetic general term

edges.reason: The arithmetic general-term formula uses the initial term and common difference defined by an arithmetic sequence.
Arithmetic formulas offer familiar indexed statements for induction practice. A telescoping reciprocal identity or other integer proposition can be proved without arithmetic-sequence formulas.
edges.scope: familiar identities used as induction exercises

edges.reason: The criteria expressly find common factors and reduce until numerator and denominator are coprime. These are the common-factor contents of the endpoint; finding the greatest factor in a single step is only a shortcut and is outside this required scope.
edges.scope: Finding a shared divisor and recognizing the absence of a shared divisor above one when reducing to simplest form

edges.reason: Reduction replaces numerator and denominator by division by the same common factor, using the value-preserving fraction property.
edges.scope: dividing numerator and denominator by a common number
